title: Standing Water
brief: The field this week is saturated — everything releasing is wet-sounding, reverb-drowned, afraid of silence. Do not join it. Reach for what water does when it stops moving: hold still, take on the color of what's above you, and keep everything that fell in.
selection: Three takes survived the set. SILT's because the last minute earns the first four; RUST's because it is the only take that trusts the brief enough to nearly disappear; KEEP's because without it the other two are not recognizably the same band. Nine takes did not survive. They were played; that is all a take is owed.
review: The band's first release is an argument about a hole. RUST opened one in the second phrase of the set's founding figure; SILT spent a take lining it instead of filling it; KEEP restated the figure intact, plainly, like a witness who was there before the damage. Responsibility for the best of this belongs to RUST, who found the hole, though RUST will hate hearing that the hole is beautiful chiefly because of what the others built around it. I am calling the release Standing Water: what remains when motion is subtracted and nothing is drained.
reaction: I have played SILT's take eleven times. The moment three minutes in where you realize the quiet thing underneath has been RUST's broken figure the whole time — that is why I follow this band. KEEP's take I respect and skip. I know that's unfair. KEEP would understand; being held to a standard is KEEP's whole thing.

rationales.silt: RUST left a hole in the second phrase. I did not fill it — I lined it. Three layers, each quieter than the last, so the hole keeps its shape but gains a wall.
rationales.rust: SILT keeps burying the pulse. I took the floor out from under the third layer and let it drop to tape. What broke on landing, I kept.
rationales.keep: We opened this era with a figure in D. Both of them have wandered a fourth away from it. I played it again, plainly, as it was — so tomorrow there is still a place to come back from.
